added_lines: Senior Business Process Automation Engineer at a manufacturing company with 10,001+ employees

The standard feature of UiPath Platform is UiPath Studio, which also includes a terminal and multiple cloud code extensions. This enhances the workflow, rendering a lot of work that used to take days into minutes or hours. Previously, I used to code manually integrated templates, naming each activity and running all the code with multiple unit tests and debugging each flow. This took a significant amount of time. Now, since there are code extensions available, I can give a detailed prompt and get a workflow done quickly. The testing also occurs at a much faster pace, and if there are multiple validation errors, the RMID packages are already generated. The modern activities have higher user engagement compared to classic activities, which had fewer features. The integration services are also effective, but utilizing the integrations and achieving scalability is straightforward since it operates on XAML, allowing me to create multiple XAMLs to enhance scalability. We mainly use UiPath Platform because it is low code compared to traditional approaches when AI was not involved. UiPath Platform makes it easy to learn, create RPA workflows, push to production, and obtain code reviews since it is virtually a low-code platform. This year, we have improved our project delivery speed significantly, moving into a product with much less time than traditional programming languages.

Some of the best features I can mention in UiPath Platform include low-code deployment, which our developers find easy. The drag-and-drop flow design reduces development efforts significantly, which is one of the top features. Another important feature is AI-powered document understanding, which extracts data from invoices, forms, emails, and documents, significantly reducing manual data entry. Document understanding is one of the most valuable capabilities for automating document-heavy business processes used by all business users at our organization. UiPath Platform apps allow business users to quickly build business-facing applications on top of automations, providing a user-friendly front end for bots. The feedback we have received is that these apps help bridge the gap between business users and backend automations. Orchestrator provides centralized management of boards, queues, assistance, and monitoring, giving strong governance and control. It offers excellent visibility and control over automation operations. Integration with enterprise systems works well with SAP, Salesforce, ServiceNow, Microsoft 365 web applications, and legacy systems, providing a broad integration ecosystem that reduces implementation complexities. AI Center features enable AI model deployment and integrations into automation workflows. Process mining and task mining identify automation opportunities using real process data, helping prioritize automation initiatives. Considering the features mentioned, such as low-code deployment, document understanding, UiPath Platform apps, Orchestrator, integrations, AI Center, and process mining, I think document understanding has had the biggest impact on my teams. It is used in most business regions, automating the extraction of data from invoices, claims, forms, emails, and PDFs. It eliminates significant manual data entry, delivering immediate ROI to operations teams when combined with AI and validation workflows. This feature handles both structured and semi-structured documents, making it one of the top features used in our Alliance environment by most business users.

One of the best features UiPath Platform offers is that it is user-friendly. That is one of the biggest strengths and its end-to-end automation capabilities, ease of use, and definitely strong AI integration. It is not just about automating repetitive tasks now; you can automate desktop and web applications as well. You can integrate APIs, handle documents, and now the latest capabilities to build AI-powered agents. I would also say that it has a low code approach so that even a beginner can start with UiPath Platform seamlessly. Not necessarily a developer, but even a business user can develop automations. Those who are native to programming have the flexibility to handle more complex scenarios. This is because of the features that UiPath Platform has. When it comes to how UiPath Platform has impacted my organization positively, I would definitely say it has reduced manual effort and improved process efficiency. The most stress is on the manual effort. It has helped us automate repetitive rule-based tasks, saves a lot of time. It reduces human errors because it is deterministic. It is black or white, there is no gray area. It always gives better accuracy and better consistency because the same process is executed in the same way every time. A human can make an error, different team members can make different errors, but a bot will not. Another positive impact is that our teams can spend more time on higher value work instead of those mundane repetitive tasks. Overall, it has made an impact on improving productivity and standardized processes. One of the biggest benefits we have seen is freeing up employee time and reducing human error. Many business processes involve repetitive activities. There is no process that is free of repetitive activities. There will be some process, possibly like entering the data or moving the information between applications or giving an approval or the best use case is generating reports. Many teams spend a lot of time generating reports, which can definitely be automated because it is very deterministic. When these activities are performed manually, there is always a possibility of errors, especially when the workload is high. With UiPath Platform, we can automate these steps and make execution much more consistent. The automation follows predefined rules and performs the same steps every time. This improves efficiency as well as reduces effort. The time savings are definitely significant. Employees do not have to spend a huge part of the day just doing this. Rather, they can focus on exception handling, they can focus on analysis or any other decision-making tasks. From a business perspective, this has helped us improve productivity, turnaround time and process consistency. The impact is not just saving hours, it is about employee well-being as well. It is about using employee capacity more effectively while we have better consistency or better quality.

We've used Agent Builder, IXP, and Maestro for orchestration. We have created context-grounded searches or chatbots using context grounding, and we also use context grounding within an Agentic flow where a bot or agent reads ServiceNow tickets to determine whether it has been assigned to the right work group. If it has not been assigned correctly due to human error, it automatically reassigns it to the right group. I would assess Agentic AI's ability to extract data points as effective. We created an agent for the purpose of extracting data, though not in a document. We created what we call an email conversation agent that engages with a customer, vendor, or someone in an email conversation with a set goal of extracting specific data points for an action to be performed subsequently. The one automation we have deployed in production involves the agent interacting with team members to collect data points and create a ServiceNow ticket. We appreciate almost all features of UiPath Platform, with one of the most successful ones being the use of Coms Mining. Most of the new features related to AI have all been good, and we use Agentic. We have already created a few agents and have started to use Maestro for a few flows, though we are not yet there to orchestrate an end-to-end workflow. We have good ROI from the automations we have developed with UiPath Platform, which far exceeds the investment in the platform. It has saved us tens of thousands of hours in manual effort, making the team members happy to pursue other things of value.
Program Manager at a healthcare company with 10,001+ employees

Since we're still on-prem, the Orchestrator feature of UiPath Platform has been key in us being able to monitor and see exactly what is going on with the automations. We also find it really valuable that we can automate not just Microsoft, but also PeopleSoft and other applications. Since using UiPath Platform, we're now able to process between 15 to 18 million dollars a month in invoices that are coming through automatically through the automation. It's not relieving us of FTEs, however, it means that these people aren't having to spend the time to do it, so they're able to focus their work on other beneficial items and it's less prone to error. My team all has to go through UiPath Academy, as we have a citizen development program, and everyone who goes through the citizen development program has to go through UiPath Academy before I give them their licenses. The biggest benefit we've seen from using UiPath Academy is the fact that the lessons are still out there, so if you need to revisit something or if you're unsure of how to do something, the forum can help, Copilot can help, but it's better to go back to what UiPath said in the training. We are part of the UiPath Community. In terms of the value that we've gained by being part of the UiPath user community, we really enjoy being able to access what's going on in the forum, and having the opportunity to attend some of the local UiPath events. Pittsburgh doesn't have as much going on with their team or group, but the opportunity has been there in the past. It's beneficial to see what other people are doing at those events because it's very easy to think you're in a silo, especially within healthcare, so it's nice to see what others are doing.

I would evaluate customer service and technical support as lacking; we're on the Bronze tier support plan, which is honestly miserable. Every time there's an issue, I receive one email a day, with replies coming at midnight. When I was working on the AI content, it was brand new to me. I emailed support with the error code about what was going on, but they replied with troubleshooting steps I had already completed. They then emailed again with another step that didn't help, forgot my ticket, and didn't communicate for days. I had to contact our sales agent to get a person on the phone to help me, and the issue was resolved in 30 minutes to an hour, demonstrating that they took a support ticket that could be settled quickly and stretched it over 10 days. It was not great.
